score.rationale:
## 1. Summary verdict
REWORK (task-requested label). Canonical CLI mapping: rejected.

## 2. Options-Considered structure check
FAIL (auto-reject). The proposal presents exactly one design ("Approach A") with no "## Options Considered" section, no "### Option N:" entries, and no "Why rejected:" lines for alternatives. Per the architecture-advisory quality bar this alone forces a non-approve verdict regardless of content quality. Missing alternatives that should have been vetted: (a) feedback-loop-only launch with LOAD gated behind a warm-up metric, (b) unify profile/feedback under the existing @astragenie/memory-provider abstraction vs bypass it, (c) block on astramem-local#184 (repo-provenance) vs an explicit documented deferral with the consequence stated.

## 3. Strengths
- Deterministic "corrections" block (agent's own memories later invalidated/superseded) is not subject to the Laplace usefulness-ranking flaw, so it is a genuinely more defensible source of day-one value than "top_lessons".
- Reuses proven FEAT-188 conventions: fail-silent, byte-identical-when-disabled, same 4 dispatch sites, .claude/loop.json-driven config, low blast-radius rollout mechanism consistent with how recall was shipped.
- The injected-atoms/runId.json sidecar gives an auditable, durable link between what was injected and later feedback, matching this repo's stated preference for inspectable artifacts over implicit memory.

## 4. Inversion findings
Option 1 - chosen (ship LOAD + feedback together): At 10x fleet/repo scale, the gate-PASS backstop's exposure bias (whatever gets injected tends to get marked "used" regardless of causal contribution) compounds - high-injection-frequency lessons entrench and newer/corrective lessons never accumulate enough signal to unseat them, so top_lessons ossifies early. Combined with the daemon's agent-only (no project) scoping, a fleet spanning many unrelated repos sees cross-repo lesson bleed grow directly with repo count, degrading signal-to-noise
